analysis: Integration of all eight units. The only functional change is provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Coordinator/ChunkBatcher.swift line ~102: `guard self.sink != nil else { return }` inside the enqueue closure on the serial queue. Frames enqueued while no session is bound are now dropped before entering `pending`. This closes a path where a deferred flush could deliver a stale frame to a replacement session after reconnect. It is a strict tightening relevant to TB-002, T-008 and A-001, and the frames are already per-request encrypted. The rest is a changelog entry, a docs update to docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump and a paragraph at head lines ~1287-1300), and a new test file (ChunkBatcherLifecycleTests.swift). The tests use unstarted NWConnection objects to 127.0.0.1:9 and bounded 10s semaphore waits, with no production effect. Docs accurately state the residual gap: SendHandle/ChunkSender persist across reconnects, so a frame from an old request processed after a new sink binds still passes the check, because there is no request-to-session identity enforcement. That gap pre-dates this PR and is not a regression. No new authorization, key, attestation or data-exposure surface was identified. The guard cannot deadlock, since flush uses queue.sync and is not called from the queue. Open item outside the supplied evidence: whether the coordinator rejects chunks for unknown or cancelled request IDs on the new session, and the ordering of ProviderLoop+Cancellation versus rebind. The sources for CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift and SendHandle were not supplied. This is recorded as an unverified contract, not a finding. The T-041 prefix-cache definition is unaffected.
